summary: Intel announced its ~$20B (later $28B) 'Ohio One' semiconductor fab complex in New Albany/Licking County, OH in January 2022, with production originally slated for late 2025. Most recent status (Axios Columbus, May 2026): construction is underway with the 'go vertical' milestone reached, but first-fab production has slipped to ~2031.

Ford and SK On announced the BlueOval City battery plant in Stanton, TN in September 2021 (part of an $11.4B multi-plant plan; the Tennessee site ~$5.6B, thousands of promised jobs). Most recent status (Tennessee Lookout, May 2026): the BlueOval SK joint venture was dissolved and SK On took full ownership of the Tennessee battery plant; construction is complete but the plant is not yet producing, with output now slated to begin around 2028.

Steel Dynamics announced a ~$1.9B electric-arc-furnace flat-roll steel mill (3M-ton capacity, ~600 direct jobs) in Sinton, TX in July 2019. Most recent status (SDI Q4/full-year 2025 results): the Sinton Flat Roll Division is in full operation, running at high capacity rates (86%+ in Q1 2025) and contributing to record company steel shipments in 2025.

Eli Lilly announced a $1B parenteral (injectable) products and devices manufacturing facility in Concord (Cabarrus County), NC in January 2022, with ~600 promised jobs. Most recent status: the site opened in mid-2024, began commercial production and shipped its first medicines by end of 2024, and as of 2026 is operational with total investment grown to ~$2B and employment exceeding 750.

Qcells (Hanwha) announced a ~$2.5B vertically integrated solar manufacturing factory in Cartersville (Bartow County), GA in January 2023, part of a plan to create ~2,500 new jobs in northwest Georgia. Most recent status (pv magazine USA, June 2026): the Cartersville plant began solar cell production, with module assembly at full capacity and full ingot/wafer/cell production expected by Q3 2026.

TSMC announced in May 2020 its intention to build an advanced semiconductor fab in Phoenix, AZ (~$12B, 5nm, ~1,600 direct jobs, production targeted 2024). As of a March 2026 report, the first Arizona fab is in high-volume production (N4, since late 2024) and the second fab is targeting 3nm mass production as early as 2H 2027.

Hyundai Motor Group announced its Metaplant America EV/hybrid assembly plant in Bryan County, GA on May 20, 2022 (~$5.54B, ~8,100 direct jobs, production targeted 2025). As of a June 2026 report the plant is operational, producing the Hyundai Ioniq 5, Ioniq 9 and Kia Sportage hybrid, ramping toward 500,000 units/year annual capacity.

Formosa Petrochemical (Sunshine Project) was announced in 2018 for a ~$9.4B, 14-plant petrochemical/plastics complex in St. James Parish, LA (~1,200 direct jobs). As of a February 2026 report, the facility remains unbuilt: major construction has been on hold since November 2020 and the project is in ongoing permit litigation, not cancelled.

Chobani announced on April 22, 2025 a $1.2B dairy processing plant at the Triangle Site in Rome (Oneida County), NY, promising 1,000+ direct jobs. As of an Aug 13, 2026 update the project is delayed: after an April 2025 groundbreaking, early site work is underway but Phase 1 production is now slated to begin between spring 2027 and summer 2028.

Anduril Industries announced its 'Arsenal-1' autonomous-weapons manufacturing facility in Pickaway County, OH (near Rickenbacker Airport) on Jan 16, 2025, committing ~$910M capital and ~4,000 direct jobs by 2035, with production targeted July 2026. As of a March 2026 report the plant has begun producing the Fury autonomous combat drone, ahead of the original timeline, with Roadrunner, Barracuda and a classified platform expected by end of 2026.

Samsung Electronics announced a ~$17B advanced semiconductor fab in Taylor (Williamson County), TX in November 2021, promising 2,000+ direct jobs with an originally targeted second-half-2024 start. As of the most recent reporting (TrendForce, March 2026) the fab is in trial operations and full-scale mass production has slipped to early 2027.

Panasonic Energy announced a ~$4B EV battery manufacturing plant in De Soto (Johnson County), KS in July 2022, promising up to 4,000 direct jobs on the former Sunflower Army Ammunition Plant site. As of the most recent reporting (KCTV5, June 2026) the plant is operational and producing EV battery cells, with additional lines and a planned data-center battery expansion underway.

Scout Motors (backed by Volkswagen) announced a ~$2B electric truck and SUV assembly plant in Blythewood (Richland County), SC in March 2023, promising 4,000 direct jobs and an originally targeted 2026 start of production. As of the most recent update (Scout Motors, July 2026) the plant is still in construction and production-readiness, with customer production now expected in 2028.

Eli Lilly announced in May 2022 a ~$2.1B investment in new pharmaceutical manufacturing at the LEAP Innovation District in Lebanon (Boone County), IN (later expanded well beyond that) to make active ingredients and new therapeutic modalities. As of the most recent reporting (WFYI, May 6, 2026) its first facility, Lilly Lebanon Advanced Therapies, has opened and is producing medicines including Zepbound and Mounjaro, with further facilities under construction. (This is a distinct Indiana site, separate from Lilly's Concord, NC plant.)

Nucor announced in January 2022 a greenfield sheet steel mill at Apple Grove in Mason County, WV (initially ~$2.7B, later ~$3.1B and up to ~$4B), promising roughly 800 full-time direct jobs and a 3-million-ton/year capacity. As of the most recent reporting (Steel Market Update, April 2026) the mill is about 85% complete with commissioning running through 2026 and commercial shipments expected to begin in early 2027. (Distinct from Steel Dynamics' Sinton, TX mill.)

Micron announced on Oct 4, 2022 an investment of up to $100B (first phase ~$20B) to build a semiconductor memory (DRAM) megafab in Clay (Onondaga County), NY, promising ~9,000 direct Micron jobs. Most recent status (Micron press release, July 9, 2026): broke ground Jan 2026 and poured first concrete for the first of four fabs, reported to be running ahead of schedule.

Rivian announced in December 2021 a ~$5B electric-vehicle assembly plant in the Stanton Springs North site near Social Circle (Walton/Morgan counties), GA, promising ~7,500 direct jobs and production originally targeted for 2024. Most recent status (Atlanta Journal-Constitution, Aug 2026): after a 2024 pause, Rivian held a Sept 2025 groundbreaking, began vertical construction in May 2026 and reports construction 'progressing well,' with production now expected in late 2028.

FUJIFILM Diosynth Biotechnologies announced in March 2021 a ~$2B large-scale cell-culture (biologics/monoclonal antibody) manufacturing facility in Holly Springs (Wake County), NC, promising ~725 direct jobs (later expanded, total site ~$3.2B). Most recent status (Fujifilm Biotechnologies grand-opening release, Sept 24, 2025): Phase 1 site opened commercially with 8 x 20,000L bioreactors and ~680+ employees, with drug-product/finished-goods lines coming online in early 2026.

Honda and LG Energy Solution announced on Oct 11, 2022 a joint-venture lithium-ion EV battery cell plant (L-H Battery Company) in Fayette County near Jeffersonville, OH, committing $3.5B (overall ~$4.4B) and ~2,200 direct jobs, with mass production originally targeted for end of 2025. Most recent status (L-H Battery Company release, July 1, 2026): the completed facility began mass production, employing 1,000+ associates, and has shifted its initial output to energy-storage-system (ESS) cells (plus hybrid-vehicle cells) rather than the originally planned EV batteries.

Chevron Phillips Chemical and QatarEnergy announced on Nov 15, 2022 the ~$8.5B Golden Triangle Polymers integrated petrochemical facility (2.08M tpa ethane cracker plus two HDPE polyethylene units) in Orange (Orange County), TX, promising 500+ direct full-time jobs, with operations originally targeted for 2026. Most recent status (BIC Magazine, May 14, 2026): the plant is in its commissioning and startup phase, with full operation expected in 2027.

Texas Instruments announced (Nov 2021, groundbreaking May 2022) a semiconductor 300mm wafer fab campus in Sherman, TX of up to ~$30B and up to 3,000 direct jobs (four fabs SM1-SM4). Most recent status: first fab SM1 began production in December 2025, ramping to volume by customer demand.

Eli Lilly announced on Dec 5, 2024 a ~$3B expansion of its recently acquired injectables (Mounjaro/Zepbound) pharmaceutical manufacturing facility in Pleasant Prairie, Kenosha County, WI, promising 750 direct jobs. Most recent facility-specific status: Pleasant Prairie granted final site-plan approval on March 17, 2025 with construction underway and the additions targeted for completion around March 2026 (freshest site-specific update found).

Toyota announced on Dec 6, 2021 its first North American automotive battery plant (Toyota Battery Manufacturing North Carolina, TBMNC) at the Greensboro-Randolph Megasite in Liberty (Randolph County), NC, initially ~$1.29B and 1,750 direct jobs, later expanded to ~$13.9B and 5,100 jobs. Most recent status: Toyota announced the start of battery production at the plant on Nov 12, 2025 (batteries began shipping June 2025).

U.S. Steel announced on Jan 11, 2022 a ~$3B greenfield steel mill ('Big River 2' / BR2, 'Project Blueprint') at its Big River Steel Works in Osceola (Mississippi County), AR, promising ~900 direct jobs and ~3 million tons/yr of new capacity. Most recent status: a U.S. Steel update dated Dec 15, 2025 states BR2 is completed and operational, roughly doubling campus capacity to ~6 million tons/yr, with full ramp targeted into 2026.

First Solar announced in November 2022 a ~$1.1B vertically integrated photovoltaic solar module manufacturing factory at the Mallard Fox West Industrial Complex in Lawrence County (Trinity), AL, promising 700+ direct jobs and 3.5 GW annual capacity. Most recent status: First Solar inaugurated the facility on Sept 26, 2024, bringing it into operation (freshest update found).

Novo Nordisk announced on June 24, 2024 a ~$4.1B second fill/finish (aseptic + finished product) pharmaceutical manufacturing facility on its Clayton campus in Johnston County, NC, adding 1.4M sq ft and 1,000 direct jobs. Most recent status (trade project profile, 2025): early clearing/foundational work underway, with completion staged 2027-2029 and opening targeted ~2029.

SK hynix announced on April 3, 2024 an ~$3.87B advanced chip-packaging fabrication and R&D facility (first U.S. HBM packaging base) at Purdue Research Park in West Lafayette, IN, with ~1,000 direct jobs. Most recent status (Purdue newsroom, Aug 27, 2026): ceremonial groundbreaking held, construction begun; investment now cited as >$4B, cleanroom/mass production targeted 2028-2029.

ExxonMobil and SABIC announced on April 19, 2017 the selection of San Patricio County (Gregory), TX for the Gulf Coast Growth Ventures petrochemical complex — a world-scale ethane steam cracker feeding two polyethylene units and a monoethylene glycol unit, a multi-billion-dollar (~$10B) investment with ~600 direct jobs. Most recent status (SABIC release, Jan 20, 2022): plant started up ahead of schedule in late 2021, in full operation and directly employing 600+; it has run at volume since (a TCEQ 2024 annual operational report is on file).

Foxconn announced in 2017 (Wisconsin site confirmed Oct 5, 2017) a ~$10B, 20-million-sq-ft flat-panel LCD display factory in Mount Pleasant, Racine County, WI, promising up to 13,000 jobs. Most recent status (The Daily Reporter, Nov 26, 2025): the campus is a far smaller operational plant now making data/AI servers, with ~$717M actually invested and 1,242 jobs as of 2024; Foxconn announced an additional $569M expansion and 1,374 more jobs (total ~$1.2B/2,616 jobs through 2029).

Mazda and Toyota announced on Jan 10, 2018 a joint-venture auto assembly plant (Mazda Toyota Manufacturing) in Huntsville, AL — an initial ~$1.6B investment, up to 4,000 direct jobs, and 300,000 vehicles/year capacity (Toyota Corolla Cross + Mazda CX-50). Most recent status I could directly confirm (Business Alabama, Mar 29, 2024): plant fully operational since 2021, reached its 4,000-employee commitment in 2023, investment raised to ~$2.3B, both models in production at up to 300k/yr capacity.

Wanhua Chemical announced on April 10, 2017 a ~$1.12B MDI/isocyanates chemical manufacturing complex in Louisiana (later sited at Convent, St. James Parish, LA), with 170 direct jobs promised. Most recent available status: the company withdrew its St. James land-use permit application on Sep 4, 2019 and the complex was not built at that site.

Wolfspeed announced on Sep 9, 2022 the John Palmour Manufacturing Center (the JP), a ~$5B, ~1,800-job silicon carbide materials facility producing 200mm SiC wafers in Siler City, Chatham County, NC. Most recent status (article updated Feb 16, 2026): facility reached production readiness in late 2025 and is growing its first 200mm SiC crystals and delivering preliminary wafers, after a delayed June 2025 start; Wolfspeed emerged from Chapter 11 restructuring in late 2025 and is ramping slowly.

Kikkoman Foods announced on April 23, 2024 (groundbreaking June 12, 2024) a ~$560M, 240,000-sq-ft greenfield soy sauce and seasonings production plant in Jefferson, Jefferson County, WI, with ~80+ new direct jobs and first soy sauce shipments targeted for fall 2026. Most recent status found (local press, July 20, 2025): plant still under construction, opening targeted for fall 2026.

Emirates Global Aluminium announced on May 16, 2025 a ~$4B primary aluminum smelter (later a 60/40 JV with Century Aluminum, ~750,000 tonnes/yr) at the Tulsa Port of Inola, Rogers County, OK, promising ~1,000 direct jobs — the first new U.S. primary aluminum smelter since 1980 (sector: other). Most recent status (Manufacturing Dive, June 5, 2026): still in initial development phase, no construction started, undergoing state environmental review; Oklahoma AG filed a June 2, 2026 suit to block it (remanded to state court on Sep 3, 2026).

Nucor announced on March 29, 2019 a steel plate mill (initially ~$1.35B, later ~$1.7B) with 400+ direct jobs and 1.2M tons/yr capacity at Buttermilk Falls Industrial Park in Brandenburg, Meade County, KY. Most recent status (Steel Market Update, Oct 28, 2025): the mill rolled first plate in Dec 2022 and has been operating since, ramping faster than anticipated and EBITDA-positive for a second consecutive quarter.

Johnson & Johnson announced on Oct 1, 2024 a >$2B advanced-technology biologics pharmaceutical manufacturing facility (~420 direct jobs) in Wilson, Wilson County, NC. Most recent status (local press, Jan 9, 2026): construction underway and hiring of advanced-manufacturing staff ramping up; targeted operational ~2028.

Shintech (Shin-Etsu subsidiary) announced on July 24, 2018 a ~$1.49B expansion at its Plaquemine, Iberville Parish, LA complex, building new chlor-alkali, vinyl chloride monomer and PVC production units (120 new direct jobs). Most recent status (trade press, late 2024): the new 380,000 t/yr PVC plant came online in Oct 2024 and Shintech added over 900 million lb/yr of PVC capacity by Dec 2024, after delays from the original early-2021 target.

Ford announced on Feb 13, 2023 a ~$3.5B lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) battery cell plant, BlueOval Battery Park Michigan, on the Marshall Megasite in Calhoun County, MI, initially ~2,500 jobs (a distinct site from Ford's BlueOval City in Stanton, TN). Most recent status (local press, 2025-2026): after a 2023 pause and downsizing to ~$3B/~1,700 jobs, construction reached the final-steel-beam milestone and the plant is on track to begin LFP production by summer 2026, with output shifted toward energy-storage cells plus a midsize EV truck.

Micron announced on Sep 1, 2022 a ~$15B leading-edge DRAM memory fab (its 'ID2' fab, ~2,000 direct jobs) in Boise, Ada County, Idaho — a distinct site from Micron's Clay/Onondaga County, NY megafab. Most recent status (local press, spring 2026): the fab reached the cleanroom 'blowdown' milestone, first-fab construction is expected to complete in 2026, and first chips are expected to roll out in 2027.

Tyson Foods announced on Nov 20, 2017 a new poultry processing complex (processing plant, hatchery and feed mill), initially ~$300M and more than 1,500 direct jobs, in Humboldt, Gibson County, TN, with operations promised for late 2019. Most recent facility-specific status found (trade press, April 2021): the complex — investment grown to ~$425M — opened in April 2021 after delay from the original late-2019 target; no site-specific update newer than 2021 was found (Tyson's 2025-2026 layoffs and closures named other plants, not Humboldt).

Samsung announced on June 28, 2017 a $380M home appliance (washing machine) manufacturing plant with 950+ direct jobs in Newberry County, SC (former Caterpillar site). Most recent status (Fox Business, Jan 21, 2025): plant operating with ~$500M invested and 1,500+ jobs, and Samsung was weighing shifting dryer production there from Mexico in response to tariffs. Sector: other (home appliances).

ArcelorMittal announced on Feb 6, 2025 a $1.2B wholly-owned non-grain-oriented electrical steel (NOES) manufacturing facility (up to 150,000 t/yr) with 200+ permanent direct jobs at Calvert (Mobile County), AL. Most recent status: facility under construction (long-lead equipment ordered, permits received, earthwork/piling underway), on track to begin production in the first half of 2027. Sector: steel.

Pratt & Whitney (RTX) announced on Oct 22, 2020 a >$650M, ~1,000,000-sq-ft turbine airfoil production facility (advanced casting foundry) with ~800 new direct jobs in Asheville (Buncombe County), NC. Most recent status (FlightGlobal, May 2025): plant opened in 2022 and is ramping, with output set to double in 2025 and a Jan 2025 $285M foundry expansion (+325 jobs) bringing total commitment to nearly $1B. Sector: aerospace and defense.

Ferrara Candy Company announced on April 22, 2026 a $675M, 750,000-sq-ft greenfield candy (NERDS/SweeTARTS/Jelly Belly) manufacturing site in Orangeburg County, SC — its first SC operation — projected to create ~1,000 jobs over 10 years, with first production lines expected in early 2029. Most recent status: Ferrara broke ground in Orangeburg in May 2026. Sector: food and beverage.

Amkor Technology announced on Nov 30, 2023 an outsourced semiconductor advanced packaging and test facility in Peoria, AZ, originally ~$2B with ~2,000 direct jobs. Most recent status: Amkor broke ground in Oct 2025 and expanded the planned campus investment to ~$7B / as many as 3,000 jobs across two phases, with first facility completion expected mid-2027 and production beginning early 2028. Sector: semiconductors.

Natron Energy announced on Aug 15, 2024 a ~$1.4B giga-scale sodium-ion battery manufacturing facility (~1,000 direct jobs, 1.2M sq ft) at the Kingsboro Megasite in Edgecombe County (Rocky Mount), North Carolina. Most recent status: Natron ceased all operations on Sep 3, 2025 amid funding shortfalls; the North Carolina factory was never constructed and is cancelled (per Construction Dive, Sep 2025).

Mercedes-Benz announced in September 2017 a ~$1B Alabama expansion to launch EV production, anchored by a new ~1M-sq-ft battery plant (up to ~600 direct jobs) at the Scott Davis Industrial Park in Bibb County (near Woodstock), Alabama. Most recent credible status found: the battery plant officially opened and began producing EV batteries for the EQS/EQE SUVs in March/April 2022 (per Business Alabama); no fresher status located.

UCB announced on March 24, 2026 a ~$2B U.S. biologics (biopharmaceutical) manufacturing campus (~330 permanent direct jobs, ~460,000 sq ft on 79 acres) at the Rowen development in Gwinnett County, Georgia. Most recent status: early/planning phase as of mid-2026, with design and construction expected to span roughly six to seven years (per pharmaceutical-technology.com); no production yet.

Fiat Chrysler (FCA, now Stellantis) announced on Feb 26, 2019 a ~$1.6B conversion of its Mack Avenue Engine Complex into a new Jeep assembly plant (Detroit Assembly Complex - Mack) with ~3,850 new direct jobs in Detroit, Michigan — the first new auto assembly plant built in Detroit in ~30 years, to build the Jeep Grand Cherokee and a three-row SUV. Most recent status (per CBT News, Apr 22, 2025): the plant is operating and building the Jeep Grand Cherokee, with temporary production pauses to transition to the refreshed 2026 model year.

Bosch announced on April 26, 2023 plans to acquire TSI Semiconductors' Roseville, California site and invest ~$1.5B (later raised to ~$2B) to convert it into a silicon carbide (SiC) semiconductor production facility, creating ~700 manufacturing/engineering/R&D direct jobs. Most recent status (per Semiconductor Today, July 2026): sample chip production has begun, the $225M CHIPS Act direct funding agreement was finalized in July 2026, and first commercial 200mm SiC chips are expected later in 2026.

Hyundai Steel announced on March 24, 2025 a $5.8B electric arc furnace (EAF)-based integrated steel mill (~1,300 direct jobs, 2.7M metric tons/yr) in Ascension Parish (RiverPlex MegaPark, near Donaldsonville), Louisiana. Most recent status: construction officially broke ground on Sept 4, 2026; commercial production targeted for 2029.

AbbVie announced on April 22, 2026 a $1.4B, 185-acre pharmaceutical manufacturing campus (small-volume parenteral drug product) in Durham, NC (near Research Triangle Park), planning to hire ~734 direct workers. Most recent status (as of the April 2026 announcement, the freshest reporting available): construction to begin in 2026 with completion targeted by end of 2028; not yet broken ground.

Braidy Industries announced on April 26, 2017 a $1.3B aluminum rolling mill (sheet/plate for auto and aerospace, ~550 direct jobs) in Greenup County (near South Shore/Ashland), Kentucky. Most recent status (freshest reporting available is 2022-2023, as the project is defunct): the mill was never built; the company (renamed Unity Aluminum) abandoned the KY site as too small, the ~205-acre property was returned to the Northeast Kentucky Regional Industrial Authority, and Kentucky recouped its $15M investment.

Ebon Solar announced on Aug 7, 2024 a projected $942M, 834,000-sq-ft solar cell manufacturing factory (~911 direct jobs) at Mesa del Sol in Albuquerque, New Mexico. Most recent status (Albuquerque Journal, early May 2026): the project was abandoned and never entered construction, with New Mexico and city officials confirming it will not move forward amid CFIUS-related concerns.

GM and LG Chem announced on Dec 5, 2019 a 50/50 joint venture (Ultium Cells LLC) to build a ~$2.3B lithium-ion EV battery cell plant (~1,100 direct jobs, 2.8M sq ft) in Lordstown, Ohio. Most recent status (mid-2026): the plant began production in 2022 (100M cells by Dec 2024) but paused cell production in January 2026 with a mass layoff of ~1,334 hourly workers; a phased return of laid-off workers was underway (July/Aug 2026) as GM/LG adjust to slower-than-expected EV demand.

Tesla announced Gigafactory Texas, a ~$1.1B+ EV auto assembly plant employing at least 5,000 in southeast Travis County near Austin, TX, in July 2020. As of the most recent reporting (May 2026) the plant is at volume, producing Model Y, Cybertruck and Cybercab.

Cree (now Wolfspeed) announced in September 2019 an ~$1B 200mm silicon carbide wafer fab (~600 jobs over eight years) at the Marcy Nanocenter in Marcy, Oneida County, NY. The Mohawk Valley Fab opened April 2022; per the most recent reporting (March 2026) it is Wolfspeed's central production hub, operating after the company emerged from Chapter 11 in September 2025. Distinct site from Wolfspeed's Siler City, NC materials plant.

SK Innovation (now SK On / SK Battery America) announced in December 2018 a $1.67B EV battery cell plant with 2,000+ jobs in Commerce, Jackson County, GA. The plant has been producing cells (e.g. for the Ford F-150 Lightning); per the most recent reporting (March 2026) it is still operating with ~1,600 workers after ~958 layoffs and is converting some lines to LFP. Distinct site from the SK On/Hyundai JV plant in Bartow County, GA.

Merck announced in July 2019 (NC Commerce) a new ~225,000-sq-ft vaccine manufacturing facility at its Maurice R. Hilleman Center in Durham, Durham County, NC, initially up to $650M and 391 jobs to make active ingredient for the Gardasil 9 HPV vaccine; the plant ultimately cost ~$1B and opened March 2025. Per the most recent reporting, Merck is winding down Gardasil production there amid falling HPV-vaccine demand, with ~154 layoffs beginning May 2026.

Leprino Foods announced in late September/October 2021 a new dairy manufacturing plant (mozzarella cheese and nutrition products) in East Lubbock, Lubbock County, TX, initially ~$870M capital (later ~$1B) and 600 jobs. It broke ground summer 2022 and opened its first phase in early 2025; per the most recent reporting (2026) it is operating and ramping toward full 600-job capacity.

Nikola Corporation broke ground July 23, 2020 on its ~$600M Coolidge, Arizona truck-assembly factory (Factory 4.0), projecting more than 1,800 jobs and ~35,000 units/year at full production. Most recent status: Nikola filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Feb 2025, and Lucid Group acquired the Coolidge factory out of the bankruptcy auction (~$30M), with court approval announced April 2025.

Texas Instruments announced RFAB2, a second 300mm analog semiconductor wafer fab in Richardson, Texas, on April 18, 2019 (>$3.1B capital, 488+ jobs). Most recent status: RFAB2 began initial production on Sep 29, 2022 and, per TI's Richardson manufacturing page, both RFAB1 and RFAB2 are in production today (~630,000 sq ft combined cleanroom).

Hanwha Q CELLS announced on May 30, 2018 a ~$150M solar module manufacturing plant in Dalton (Whitfield County), Georgia, projecting 500+ jobs and ~1.6 GW annual capacity. It held its grand opening Sep 20, 2019 and became the Western Hemisphere's largest solar panel plant. Most recent status: the Dalton factory is operating (expanded to ~5.1 GW) and resumed solar panel production in March 2026 after a temporary customs-clearance furlough.

BlueScope's board approved (announced Aug 2019) a ~US$700M expansion of its North Star mini-mill in Delta, Ohio, adding a third electric arc furnace, a second slab caster and ~850,000 tonnes/yr of hot-rolled coil capacity, with commissioning targeted for FY2022. Most recent status: the expansion was completed (ribbon-cutting May 2022) and the mill operated at full capacity (~3 million tonnes/yr) through fiscal 2024, with a further ~US$88M debottlenecking project underway.

CF Industries, with JV partners JERA and Mitsui, announced a final investment decision on April 8, 2025 for the ~$3.7B Blue Point One low-carbon ('blue') ammonia complex in Ascension Parish (Modeste), Louisiana — ~1.4 million tonnes/yr, the world's largest single ammonia plant by nameplate, with ~100 permanent jobs (~3,900 construction). Most recent status: the JV broke ground and began civil construction in August 2026, with first ammonia production targeted for 2029 (not yet producing).

General Motors announced on Jan 27, 2020 a $2.2B conversion of its Detroit-Hamtramck plant (renamed Factory ZERO) in Detroit, Michigan into its first fully all-electric vehicle assembly plant, projecting more than 2,200 jobs. Most recent status (Electrek, Apr 21, 2026): the plant has produced EVs (Hummer EV, Silverado EV, Sierra EV, Escalade IQ) since late 2021 but was idled again in March 2026 amid weak EV-truck demand, with a planned 2028 truck refresh indefinitely suspended.

First Solar announced in August 2023 a new solar module manufacturing plant near the Acadiana Regional Airport in Iberia Parish, Louisiana, committing up to $1.1 billion and 700+ new direct jobs for a 3.5 GW facility (distinct from First Solar's Lawrence County, Alabama plant). Most recent status (LED inauguration release, Nov 21, 2025): the plant began production in July 2025, several months ahead of schedule, employed 700+ (targeting 826 by year-end 2025), and is ramping toward 3.5 GW annual capacity.

Commercial Metals Company (CMC) announced in August 2020 a ~$300 million steel micro mill (Steel Arizona 2) in Mesa, Arizona, projecting ~185 direct jobs; it was billed as the world's first micro mill to produce both rebar and merchant bar quality products, targeted to open in early 2023. Most recent status (Steel Market Update, Mar 21, 2025): the mill held its grand opening in Oct 2023 and is producing but remained in a ramp-up phase through early 2025 with transformer/startup issues, with CMC's CEO expecting it to be continuously profitable in 2026.

AstraZeneca announced (as part of its July 2025 $50B U.S. plan, with the Virginia project detailed/increased to $4.5B on Oct 9, 2025) a new drug-substance manufacturing campus at Rivanna Futures in Albemarle County, Virginia, projecting ~600 permanent direct jobs. Most recent status (Aug 2026 reporting): the project remains in early stages — site preparation, grading, and utility work in 2026 with a regional workforce push underway — with manufacturing operations still several years out.

The Coca-Cola Company/fairlife announced in May 2023 a new ~$650 million dairy processing plant (about 745,000 sq ft) in Webster, Monroe County, New York, projecting several hundred direct jobs. Most recent status (New York Governor's Office / Rochester Business Journal, Aug 2026): the plant held a soft-opening ribbon-cutting on Aug 21, 2026 and is ramping production toward full operation later in 2026, having already hired roughly 380 employees.

SK Siltron CSS announced plans in August 2021 for a ~$300M silicon-carbide (SiC) wafer manufacturing plant (up to ~150 jobs) in Bay City / Monitor Township, Michigan (ribbon-cut Sept 2022). Most recent status: in mid-July 2026 SK Siltron said it would wind down its SK Siltron CSS subsidiary and close the Monitor Township site, affecting ~140 employees, citing sustained weakness in the EV/SiC market.

Ford Motor Company and SK Innovation announced on Sept 27, 2021 the ~$5.8 billion BlueOval SK Battery Park in Glendale (Hardin County), Kentucky — twin EV lithium-ion battery cell plants projected to create ~5,000 jobs, with production targeted for 2025. Most recent status: the plants launched production in Aug 2025, but after Ford and SK On agreed in Dec 2025 to end the joint venture, the Glendale battery operation closed on Feb 14, 2026 (~1,600 workers laid off); Ford is taking sole ownership and plans to convert it to grid/energy-storage battery production by late 2027.

VinFast Automotive was announced on March 29, 2022 by Gov. Roy Cooper as selecting Chatham County (Triangle Innovation Point, near Moncure), North Carolina, for the state's first auto assembly plant — an EV car/battery factory pledging an initial ~$2 billion investment (later described as ~$4 billion) and ~7,500 jobs, with production targeted for mid-2024. Most recent status: the project stalled and the site sat idle since late 2024; on May 21, 2026 North Carolina sued VinFast for missing construction and job deadlines, seeking to reclaim the ~1,765-acre megasite, while VinFast has sought to restart with a scaled-back plan (~1,400 jobs, production pushed to 2028).

EVRAZ North America announced (project initiated in 2019) a new ~$500 million long-rail steel mill at its Rocky Mountain Steel plant in Pueblo, Colorado — billed as the largest solar-powered steel mill in the U.S. (powered by the adjacent 300 MW Bighorn Solar array) and projected to employ ~300 once operational; it broke ground in early 2022. Most recent status (as of a July 16, 2025 report): the mill is operational and producing steel, and its owner EVRAZ North America was being acquired by private-equity firm Atlas Holdings in a deal valued up to ~$500 million, expected to close later in 2025.

Illuminate USA (a solar manufacturer backed by Invenergy) was announced in March 2023 to build a solar module manufacturing plant in a 1.1-million-sq-ft facility in Pataskala (Licking County), Ohio — an investment of over ~$600 million projecting ~850 jobs initially (up to ~1,000 at full production), with ~5 GW of annual solar panel capacity. Most recent status: the plant began production in Feb 2024 and by 2025 was fully operational with 1,500+ employees, having become Pataskala's largest employer and ramping toward its full multi-line capacity.

GM and Samsung SDI announced on June 13, 2023 a >$3 billion (locally approved at ~$3.5B) EV battery cell plant in New Carlisle, Indiana (~1,600 direct jobs, 30+ GWh). Most recent status (Aug 11, 2026): GM sold its ~49.99% stake to Samsung SDI, which now wholly owns the still-under-construction plant and is pivoting it toward energy-storage-system (ESS) battery production alongside prismatic cells.

Intel announced on May 3, 2021 a $3.5 billion expansion of its Rio Rancho, New Mexico campus (Fab 9) for high-volume Foveros 3D advanced semiconductor packaging, projecting ~700 permanent jobs plus ~1,000 construction jobs. Most recent status: Fab 9 opened and entered volume production on Jan 24, 2024; amid Intel's 2025 company-wide cuts the site remained operational, though Intel filed a WARN notice to cut 227 of its ~3,100 New Mexico jobs by September 2025.

Volkswagen announced in January 2019 an ~$800 million expansion of its Chattanooga, Tennessee assembly plant to build electric vehicles on the MEB platform (its first North American EV site), projecting ~1,000 new jobs (groundbreaking Nov 13, 2019). Most recent status: ID.4 production began in 2022 but VW is ending U.S. ID.4 assembly at Chattanooga by mid-April 2026 amid weak EV demand, retooling the line for the redesigned 2027 Atlas.

JSW Steel USA announced on June 22, 2018 a plan to invest up to $500 million (two phases) to acquire, restart and modernize the idled Acero Junction electric-arc-furnace flat-steel mill in Mingo Junction, Ohio, projecting several hundred (~500) direct jobs at the site. Most recent status: the EAF is operating — the plant cast its first slab in Dec 2018, resumed melting in March 2021 after a 2020 idle, and per Global Energy Monitor produced ~890,000 tonnes in 2024.

Thermo Fisher Scientific announced on Dec 10, 2020 an ~$500 million expansion of its Greenville, North Carolina pharmaceutical campus for sterile drug-product development and commercial manufacturing of medicines, therapies and vaccines (including a new 130,000-sq-ft building with two live-virus filling lines), projecting ~500 new jobs. Most recent status (Pharma Manufacturing, June 6, 2025): the site is operational as Thermo Fisher's North American flagship sterile fill-finish facility with ~2,000 employees, with new fill-finish and continuous-manufacturing lines qualified/coming online and its first commercial continuous-manufacturing product slated for 2025.

Nestlé Purina PetCare announced on Oct 26, 2020 a $550M dry pet food factory (~300+ jobs) in Williamsburg Township, Clermont County, Ohio. Per a WCPO report dated Aug 31, 2026, the plant held its grand opening and is now producing, with 430+ associates and plans for 500+.

Blue Origin announced in June 2017 (with a ~$200M investment and 300+ jobs detailed at the Jan 2019 construction launch) its Engines Factory rocket-engine plant at Cummings Research Park in Huntsville, Alabama. Per a WAFF report dated May 7, 2026, the 350,000-sq-ft Engines Factory opened in early 2020 and produces BE-4 engines (powering New Glenn and ULA's Vulcan) and BE-3U; Blue Origin now employs 1,600+ across three Huntsville sites.

Siemens announced on Aug 7, 2026 a new ~$185M, 550,000-sq-ft manufacturing facility (~1,400 jobs) at 580 Raco Parkway in Pendergrass, Jackson County, Georgia, to make low-voltage electrical infrastructure products for data centers. As of the Aug 2026 reporting it is pre-construction — buildout is slated to begin November 2026 with hiring in 2027, subject to final approvals.

Nucor announced on Sept 7, 2018 a ~$650M modernization/expansion of its Nucor Steel Gallatin flat-rolled sheet mill in Ghent (Gallatin County), Kentucky, roughly doubling capacity toward ~3M tons/yr. The mill produced its first coil after the upgrade on June 24, 2022; the most recent detailed status found (2023) reports the expansion fully online at capacity with 700+ employees.

Eastman announced on Jan 29, 2021 a ~$250M world-scale plastic-to-plastic molecular recycling (methanolysis) facility at its Kingsport, Tennessee site, converting waste polyester into DMT/MEG feedstock (~110,000 t/yr). It reached initial production in March 2024; a Chemical Processing report dated June 3, 2025 describes the Kingsport facility as currently operating and scaling up.

GlobalWafers, through subsidiary GlobiTech, announced in June 2022 a ~$5B 300mm silicon-wafer manufacturing plant (up to ~1,500 jobs) in Sherman, Texas. As of the most recent update (grand opening, May 15, 2025), Phase One construction is complete and undergoing equipment installation; the plant held its ribbon-cutting/grand opening.

Rivian announced in January 2017 the purchase and retooling of the former Mitsubishi auto-assembly plant in Normal, Illinois to build EVs, initially projecting 500 jobs (1,000+ at full volume) and growing capital investment. As of the most recent reporting (May 2026), the plant is in full production of R1 trucks/SUVs and commercial vans and is ramping the new R2 line, employing several thousand.

Siemens Gamesa announced in October 2021 a ~$200M offshore wind-turbine blade manufacturing factory (~310 direct jobs) at the Portsmouth Marine Terminal in Portsmouth, Virginia, to supply Dominion's CVOW project. As of the most recent status (November 2023), the project was cancelled/discontinued and never built, with the company citing unmet development milestones.

Amgen announced in August 2021 the selection of Holly Springs, North Carolina for a new ~$550M drug-substance biomanufacturing facility, projecting ~355 direct jobs. As of the most recent status, Amgen held the facility's ribbon-cutting/opening on January 24, 2025 (with a further ~$1B expansion announced in Dec 2024 that would raise total jobs toward ~700).

Boom Supersonic announced on Jan 26, 2022 the selection of Piedmont Triad International Airport in Greensboro, North Carolina for its Overture Superfactory, a supersonic-airliner assembly plant, promising more than 1,750 direct jobs by 2030 (2,400+ by 2032). As of the most recent facility status (construction completed June 17, 2024), the ~180,000-sq-ft factory building is finished and being fitted with assembly tooling; no Overture aircraft have yet been produced there.

StarPlus Energy (Stellantis + Samsung SDI JV) announced in May 2022 its first U.S. lithium-ion EV battery plant in Kokomo, Indiana, an over-$2.5B investment (up to ~$3.1B) with ~1,400 direct jobs. Most recent status (Inside Indiana Business, Feb 2025): the first plant opened its initial production line in Dec 2024, with remaining lines ramping through 2025.

Ford announced in September 2020 a new ~$700M, 500,000-sq-ft Rouge Electric Vehicle Center at its Rouge complex in Dearborn, Michigan to build the all-electric F-150 Lightning, adding ~300 direct jobs, with production targeted for mid-2022. Most recent status (Ford Authority, Oct 24, 2025): F-150 Lightning production at the plant, which began in 2022, is paused indefinitely as Ford reprioritizes gas/hybrid trucks.

Intel announced in March 2021 a ~$20B expansion at its Ocotillo campus in Chandler, Arizona to build two new leading-edge chip factories, Fab 52 and Fab 62, creating more than 3,000 direct jobs. Most recent status (Arizona Technology Council / Phoenix Business Journal, Oct 9, 2025): Fab 52 is Intel's first U.S. 18A-process fab and is ramping toward high-volume Panther Lake production later in 2025; Fab 62 follows roughly a year behind.

Lamb Weston announced in July 2021 a ~$415M expansion of its American Falls, Idaho plant, adding a new french fry processing line (raising capacity ~40%) plus cold storage, with ~130-280 direct jobs. Most recent status (PotatoPro, Aug 2024): the expanded french fry line held its grand opening on Aug 12, 2024 and is operational.

Nucor announced on March 12, 2018 a ~$240M rebar micro mill in Frostproof (Polk County), Florida, with ~250 direct jobs and ~350,000 tons/yr capacity. Most recent status: the mill reached first output and began operating in December 2020 (SteelOrbis, Dec 30, 2020) and has remained in normal operation since (a current 2026 Nucor Frostproof jobs posting confirms ongoing operations).

Nissin Foods USA announced in November 2023 a $228M instant-noodle manufacturing plant (Top Ramen, Cup Noodles) at 1170 Bracken Road in Piedmont, Greenville County, South Carolina, with 300+ direct jobs and operations planned to begin August 2025. Most recent status found (2025): the plant was actively hiring/staffing toward its planned Aug 2025 startup; no press report confirming first production was located as of the search.

GlobalFoundries announced on July 19, 2021 a new second semiconductor fab (Fab 8.2) at its Fab 8 campus in Malta (Saratoga County), New York — a multibillion-dollar greenfield build (alongside a $1B expansion of the existing Fab 8), projecting ~1,000 new direct jobs. Most recent status found (Malta Planning Board action, May 28, 2025): construction of Fab 8.2 remains deferred, with site-plan approval extended from July 2025 to July 2027; the separate Fab 8 upgrade backed by a Nov 2024 CHIPS award has begun, but the second fab has not started.

Steel Dynamics announced on Nov 2, 2022 the selection of Columbus (Lowndes County), Mississippi for a new ~$2.5B (later ~$2.7B) greenfield recycled-aluminum flat-rolled mill, built under its Aluminum Dynamics unit, projecting ~700 direct jobs with startup planned in 2025. Most recent status found (2025-2026 trade reporting): the mill produced its first aluminum ingot in Jan 2025 and shipped its first coils in Q2 2025; it is now commissioning/ramping, with two of three cold mills producing prime product and a third scheduled to commission in Q3 2026.

Airbus announced in October 2018 (breaking ground January 2019) a new A220 aircraft final assembly line at its Mobile, Alabama Aeroplex at Brookley campus — a ~$264 million investment projected to add 400+ direct jobs. Most recent status found (July 2025): the line is in active production, having delivered its 100th Mobile-assembled A220.

Enel North America, through its subsidiary 3Sun USA, announced in May 2023 a planned >$1 billion, 3 GW solar PV cell-and-module manufacturing factory at the Tulsa Port of Inola, Oklahoma, projecting roughly 1,000 direct jobs with first modules targeted for 2025. Most recent credible status found (Tulsa World, Oct 2024, reaffirmed in early-2025 reporting): the project remains on hold/paused while Enel seeks a majority financial partner; no more recent update was located as of the search.

Nestle Purina PetCare announced on Sept 30, 2020 a ~$450M dry pet food factory (~300+ direct jobs) in a repurposed 1.3M-sq-ft former brewery in Eden (Rockingham County), North Carolina; the plant held its official grand opening and reached production on March 26, 2024.

ExxonMobil announced on May 2, 2019 a ~$2B major chemical expansion at its Baytown, Texas complex, adding a 400,000 t/yr performance-polymers (Vistamaxx/Exact) unit and a 350,000 t/yr linear alpha olefins (Elevexx) unit; both units started up and reached production on Sept 19, 2023 (most recent status; now in full operation).

Green Bay Packaging announced in June 2018 an investment of more than $500M (~200 direct jobs) to build a new recycled testliner paper mill in Green Bay, Wisconsin, the first new paper mill in the state in over 30 years; the mill produced its first reel of paper on March 11, 2021 and was inaugurated June 2021 (most recent status; now in operation).

GM and LG Energy Solution announced on April 16, 2021 a ~$2.3B EV battery cell plant (Ultium Cells second U.S. plant; ~1,300 direct jobs) in Spring Hill, Tennessee - a distinct site from the first Ultium plant in Warren/Lordstown, Ohio. The plant began battery-cell production in 2024 and, per GM's July 14, 2025 update (most recent status), is operating and being upgraded to add LFP cell lines.

First Solar announced on June 9, 2021 a ~$680M third U.S. solar module manufacturing facility (3.3 GWdc, ~500 direct jobs) in Lake Township (Northwest Ohio), a distinct site from its later Alabama and Louisiana plants. The factory began operations in the first half of 2023 and, per the most recent status, ramped toward full nameplate capacity through 2024 into early 2025 (now producing).

Novelis broke ground in May 2022 on a greenfield low-carbon aluminum recycling and rolling mill in Bay Minette, Alabama, announced at ~$2.5B (cost later rising to ~$4.1-5B) with ~1,000 jobs and 600,000 t/yr capacity. Most recent status (2026): the plant is in commissioning, with first output/commissioning expected in 2H 2026 — not yet at volume.

Sustainable Beef LLC announced in March 2021 a new greenfield beef processing plant in North Platte, Nebraska (~$400M, ~875 direct jobs, ~550,000 sq ft), later gaining Walmart as a minority investor. Most recent status (Feb 2026): the plant, which opened May 2025, reached its target of processing 1,500 head of cattle per day and employs roughly 1,000 people — in full operation.

LG Energy Solution announced in March 2023 a ~$5.5B stand-alone battery manufacturing complex in Queen Creek, Arizona (a cylindrical EV-battery plant plus an LFP ESS-battery plant, 53 GWh total, several thousand jobs). Most recent status (2025-2026): the cylindrical EV-battery facility is nearing completion with hiring ramping toward a 2026 production start, while the ESS-battery portion was temporarily paused.

Micron announced on Aug 29, 2018 a ~$3B investment (through 2030, ~1,100 jobs) to expand memory production at its semiconductor fab in Manassas, Virginia. Most recent status (May 2026): Micron began producing 1-alpha DRAM at the Manassas fab as part of a >$2B expansion to quadruple DDR4 output — described as the most advanced memory ever made in the U.S., with full qualified production expected by end of 2026.

Canadian Solar announced on June 15, 2023 its first U.S. facility, a 5 GW solar module manufacturing plant in Mesquite, Texas (over $250M investment, ~1,500 jobs). Most recent status (2026): the plant has been operating since December 2023 with ~1,500 employees and is being expanded to 10 GW nameplate capacity, with completion expected in the second half of 2026.

GSK announced on Oct 24, 2024 an up-to-$800M expansion of its Marietta (Lancaster County), Pennsylvania pharmaceutical site, adding sterile-liquid vaccine/medicine drug-product capacity and a new vaccines drug-substance facility plus 200+ direct jobs (doubling the site). Most recent status found (BioBuzz, Sep 25, 2025): the project is in its construction/expansion phase, with the drug-substance plant targeted for end-2027 and drug-product for end-2028.

Gotion announced in September 2023 a ~$2B EV/energy-storage lithium-ion battery plant (up to ~2,600 jobs) in a converted 1.5M-sq-ft former Kmart distribution center in Manteno (Kankakee County), Illinois. Most recent status found (Shaw Local, Nov 18, 2025): the plant is producing on five lines (EV batteries, energy-storage systems, mobile chargers) with ~300 employees, targeting 450 by end-2025 and 1,400 in 2026.

Avio USA (U.S. subsidiary of Italy's Avio S.p.A.) announced on Feb 27, 2026 the selection of Hurt (Pittsylvania County), Virginia for a ~$500M, 860,000-sq-ft solid rocket motor manufacturing facility (defense/tactical propulsion, missile systems, commercial space) with 1,000+ direct jobs, at the Southern Virginia Multimodal Park. Most recent status found (Feb 2026): site selected and Virginia MEI incentive package approved; construction expected to begin in H1 2026, with no groundbreaking reported yet as of the freshest available source.

Methanex reached a final investment decision on July 19, 2019 for the ~$1.3-1.4B Geismar 3 (G3) 1.8-million-tonne/year methanol plant, built adjacent to its existing Geismar 1 & 2 units in Geismar (Ascension Parish), Louisiana. Most recent status found (Methanex FY2025 Form 40-F, filed Mar 5, 2026): G3 produced first methanol in late July 2024 and was producing during 2025 (Geismar complex output ~3,330 kt), including a restart on May 1, 2025 after an unplanned outage in late February 2025.

Corning announced in early 2024 (Michigan Strategic Fund grants approved Feb 2024; publicly detailed Oct 2024) a new solar ingot and wafer manufacturing facility in Richland Township (Saginaw County), Michigan, co-located on its Hemlock polysilicon campus, initially ~$900M with ~1,100 direct jobs (later increased toward ~$1.5B and ~1,500 jobs). Most recent status found (Solar Power World, Oct 29, 2025): the plant is online and producing solar wafers, described as the largest U.S. solar ingot/wafer facility and ramping toward over 1 million wafers per day.

L3Harris announced (April 15, 2026) a $1.265B expansion, the Virginia Advanced Propulsion Facilities, to more than double solid rocket motor production at its Orange County, VA site, creating 350+ direct jobs over five years (aerospace and defense). Distinct from the smaller $41.2M five-facility project announced April 2024. Most recent status (Manufacturing Dive, April 16, 2026): early design/construction-planning stage, working with designers and construction firms; no new facilities yet vertical.

USA Rare Earth announced (June 2, 2026) a $1.2B facility at Bailey Industrial Park in Blacksburg (Cherokee County), SC, to make sintered NdFeB permanent magnets and refined rare earth metals, creating ~490 direct jobs (sector: other manufacturing). Most recent status (Manufacturing Dive, June 3, 2026): engineering and equipment procurement underway, site work to begin 'in coming months,' commissioning targeted for 2028 (April 2028 per company).

Schwan's Company (CJ Foods/CJ CheilJedang subsidiary) announced (May 30, 2024) a ~$550M, 700,000-sq-ft Asian-food production plant at Foundation Park in Sioux Falls, SD, for the Bibigo brand, creating ~600 direct jobs (food and beverage); site first flagged in 2021 but the detailed investment/jobs commitment came in 2024. Most recent status (South Dakota Searchlight, Dec 19, 2025, read via browser UA): plant under construction, described as the largest single private investment in state history, with opening targeted for mid-2027.

Cronus Chemicals LLC announced (Aug 26, 2025, via Gov. Pritzker at the Farm Progress Show) a $2B ammonia/nitrogen-fertilizer plant near Tuscola, IL (950,000 short tons/yr, with carbon capture), ~130 direct jobs — qualifies on the $2B capital floor (chemicals and plastics). Long-planned since ~2012-2014, it moved forward in 2025 after a renewed EDGE tax agreement and 2024 EPA permits. Most recent status (FarmWeek, Aug 27, 2025): construction had not yet begun, financiers still to sign off, with imminent groundbreaking expected and ~40 months from groundbreaking to full production; no newer construction-start report found as of Sept 2026.

Industrial Electric Mfg. (IEM) announced (Aug 25, 2026) a $200M, ~1M-sq-ft power-distribution/switchgear manufacturing plant at Brooks City Base in San Antonio, TX, expected to create up to 3,000 jobs by 2030 (machinery/electrical equipment); state offered a $3.36M Texas Enterprise Fund grant tied to 448 jobs. Most recent status (Axios San Antonio, Aug 25, 2026): just announced; facility to be developed in phases with construction and hiring timelines to be released in coming months (no groundbreaking yet).

JetZero announced (June 2025) a $4.7B blended-wing-body aircraft manufacturing and final assembly campus at Piedmont Triad International Airport in Greensboro, NC, promising 14,500 jobs. Most recent status: broke ground June 15, 2026, with first-phase construction (NC Composite Center) beginning and initial deliveries targeted for the early 2030s.

The J.M. Smucker Co. announced (Nov 2021) a ~$1.1B Smucker's Uncrustables manufacturing facility at the JeffMet Industrial Complex in McCalla, Alabama, promising up to 750 jobs and production around 2025. Most recent credible status (grand opening, Nov 7, 2024): the 900,000-sq-ft plant opened and is producing, with ~370 employed at opening and hiring ramping toward 700; no more recent update located as of Sept 2026.

Eli Lilly announced (Dec 15, 2025) a >$6B active-pharmaceutical-ingredient manufacturing campus on a ~260-acre Greenbrier South site in Huntsville/Limestone County, Alabama, to make small-molecule and peptide medicines (incl. oral GLP-1s), promising 450 direct jobs. Most recent status as of Sept 2026: site selected and pre-construction; construction expected to begin in 2026 with completion targeted for 2032 — no groundbreaking reported yet.

LG Chem announced (Nov 2022) a ~$3.2B EV battery cathode (NCMA) manufacturing plant on the 420-acre Allensworth site in Clarksville (Montgomery County), Tennessee, promising ~860 jobs and initial production originally targeted for H2 2025. Most recent credible reporting located (through Sept 2026): the plant broke ground Dec 19, 2023 and is under construction, with mass production pushed to 2026 (slipped from the original H2-2025 target) to coincide with a GM cathode supply deal beginning 2026; I could not confirm a dated source establishing that first output had actually begun.

Texas Instruments announced (Feb 15, 2023) an ~$11B second 300mm analog/embedded semiconductor wafer fab (LFAB2) in Lehi, Utah, adjoining its existing LFAB1, promising ~800 direct jobs and initial production as early as 2026. Most recent status (TI's Lehi page, reflecting construction imagery through Feb 2026 and a June 2025 update): LFAB2 is still under construction and slated to begin production in 2026; no source located confirms first output has yet begun as of Sept 2026.

Absolics (an SKC/SK Group affiliate) broke ground Nov 2022 on a $600M glass-substrate semiconductor advanced-packaging plant in Covington, GA, promising 400+ jobs (backed by $75M CHIPS funding). As of 2026 the fab has completed equipment install and is in customer qualification (samples to AMD), with mass production targeted for end of 2026.

Hitachi Energy announced Sept 4, 2025 a $457M expansion in South Boston (Halifax County), VA to build what it calls the largest U.S. facility for large power transformers, promising 825 new jobs with completion targeted by 2028. As of the June 29, 2026 groundbreaking the project is in early construction; production has not yet begun.

Great Lakes Cheese broke ground (April 28, 2022) on a $518M cheese manufacturing and packaging plant in Franklinville/Farmersville, Cattaraugus County, NY, promising 215 new jobs (plus 228 retained), to replace its Cuba, NY facility. Construction finished in 2024; as of Sept 2025 the plant had resumed limited production (per WIVB). Status read via Wayback snapshot web.archive.org/web/20251013020105/ as the live WIVB page returns HTTP 403.

The U.S. Army's Universal Artillery Projectile Lines (UAPL) facility in Mesquite, TX -- a ~$576M ($500M+) artillery-projectile metal-parts plant designed, built and operated by General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems (GD-OTS) -- was inaugurated May 29, 2024, intended to help reach a 155mm output goal of 100,000 rounds/month. As of a July 14, 2026 report, the plant had not yet produced projectile parts meeting contract specification (GD-OTS committed a further $200M of its own funds in June 2026).

Boviet Solar announced (April 26, 2024) its first North American production facility in Greenville, Pitt County, NC -- a two-phase, ~$294M solar module and PV cell manufacturing plant promising ~908 jobs. As of a Jan 2026 update, the Phase I module factory has been operational since April 2025 (ramped to 3 GW), while the Phase II PV cell factory is under construction with completion targeted for the second half of 2026.

USG Corporation announced (May 14, 2026, via Gov. Abbott / Texas JETI program) a $1.175B (initial $650M) gypsum-based building-materials manufacturing facility (drywall/Sheetrock) on a former International Paper mill site in Orange, TX, creating ~200 jobs. As of the most recent reporting (May 2026) the project is newly announced; construction not yet confirmed, targeted operational by early 2028.

Lyten announced (Oct 15, 2024) plans for the world's first lithium-sulfur battery gigafactory, a >$1B, 1.25M-sq-ft plant on a 125-acre site at Reno AirLogistics Park (Stead), Nevada, employing ~200 initially (1,000+ at full scale), targeting Phase 1 in 2027. Most recent status (late Jan 2026): the Reno-Tahoe Airport Authority says lease talks with Lyten ended and the Stead site 'is not happening'; Lyten disputes that it cancelled, saying its Nevada commitment stands but the timeline has slipped after acquiring overseas (Northvolt) assets — no new site or timeline given.

Regeneron announced (Nov 13, 2025, via Gov. Hochul/Empire State Development) a >$2B biologics/sterile-injectables drug manufacturing facility on a ~1M-sq-ft former Quad Graphics site at 56 Duplainville Rd, Saratoga Springs (Saratoga County), NY, creating ~1,000 permanent jobs. Most recent status (Daily Gazette, July 27, 2026): in early redevelopment, not yet under active construction; environmental clearance/master plan approved May 2026 and Phase 1 approved June 2026, with a projected 3-5 year buildout; also selected for the FDA PreCheck pilot to speed manufacturing approvals.

SkyWater Technology announced (July 22, 2022, with the State of Indiana and Purdue) a $1.8B semiconductor R&D and fabrication facility in the Discovery Park District at Purdue in West Lafayette, Indiana, expected to create ~750 direct jobs. Most recent status (the freshest reporting available is from April 2024): SkyWater cancelled the project and released its land option after not securing CHIPS Act funding; Purdue confirmed the fab will not be built and the project is on indefinite hold. No revival reported as of Sept 2026.

Lucid Motors broke ground (Dec 2, 2019) on AMP-1, its greenfield electric-vehicle assembly plant in Casa Grande, Arizona, pledging a >$700M multi-phase investment (>$300M first phase) and thousands of jobs. Most recent status (CleanTechnica, Feb 11, 2026): AMP-1 is in production, building both the Lucid Air sedan and the Gravity SUV (Gravity entering peak production), and has been expanded to more than 3.85M sq ft as Lucid's primary U.S. manufacturing site.

Roehm (methacrylates producer) announced on June 30, 2021 a world-scale methyl methacrylate (MMA) plant in Bay City, Texas, integrated into OQ Chemicals' existing site: 250,000 t/yr (551 million lb/yr) capacity, ~70 direct jobs, and the first commercial-scale deployment of its C2-based LiMA technology. Capital clears the $100M floor as a world-scale plant (trade press, e.g. Chemical Processing, headlines it a ~$1.6B plant). Groundbreaking was Oct 27, 2022 with mechanical completion promised for 2023/early 2024. Most recent status: the plant officially opened and has reached sustained full-scale industrial operation as of June 5, 2026. Sector: chemicals and plastics.

Isuzu North America announced on Feb 12, 2025 (via SC Gov. McMaster / SC Commerce) a $280M medium-duty truck assembly plant on ~200 acres in Piedmont, Greenville County, SC -- its first U.S. production base, more than 700 direct jobs, ~50,000 trucks/yr (N-Series gas, N-Series electric, F-Series diesel). Clears both floors ($280M capital and 700 jobs). Most recent status: groundbreaking held Oct 1, 2025; the plant is under construction (a 14-18 month modification of an existing 1M-sq-ft building) with production targeted for 2027 -- not yet producing as of the latest reporting. Sector: auto assembly.

Hybar LLC (rebar startup led by Dave Stickler) selected a greenfield site in Osceola, Mississippi County, Arkansas on Nov 1, 2022 for its first electric-arc-furnace steel rebar micro-mill; the project grew to a ~$700M investment (described as the largest capital project in Arkansas history) with ~200 direct jobs and ~630,000-700,000 short-tons/yr nameplate capacity, and broke ground Aug 2, 2023. Clears both floors. Most recent status: the mill rolled its first rebar on May 28, 2025 and reached commercial production later in 2025; as of 2026 it is operating and ramping toward full capacity (positive cash-flow reported by Oct 2025). (A separate second $1.1B Hybar mill broke ground June 2026 -- not this project.) Status source read via browser user agent (arkansasbusiness.com 403s on default fetch). Sector: steel.

Envision AESC (Japanese EV-battery maker, part of Envision Group) announced on April 13, 2022 a $2B, 30 GWh EV battery-cell/module gigafactory in the Kentucky Transpark, Bowling Green (Warren County), KY, pledging ~2,000 direct jobs; it broke ground Aug 30, 2022 and reached structural completion/topping-out in Sep 2023, initially eyeing an early-2025 opening with full operation targeted for 2027. Clears both floors ($2B capital and 2,000 jobs). Most recent credible status (Bowling Green Daily News, June 9, 2025): construction/infrastructure work continuing and AESC reaffirming the $2B/2,000-job commitment -- the plant is not yet producing; its sister AESC plant in Florence, SC had construction paused (a separate site). No fresher status than June 2025 located as of Sept 2026. Sector: battery.

Merck & Co. announced and broke ground on Oct 20, 2025 (with VA Gov. Youngkin / Virginia Economic Development Partnership) a $3B 'Center of Excellence' pharmaceutical manufacturing facility -- a ~400,000-sq-ft major expansion of its long-standing Elkton (Rockingham County), Virginia site -- to produce active pharmaceutical ingredients and drug products for small-molecule medicines, pledging ~500 permanent jobs (up from a prior ~$2B/300-job plan). This is a distinct site from Merck's Durham, NC vaccine plant. Clears both floors ($3B capital and 500 jobs). Most recent status: construction began in Oct 2025 and is ongoing through 2026-2027, with initial operations/validation targeted for 2028 and commercial production toward 2029 -- not yet producing; the freshest credible update is the Oct 20, 2025 groundbreaking. Sector: pharmaceuticals.

American Battery Factory broke ground Oct 26, 2023 on a $1.2B, 2M-sq-ft lithium iron-phosphate (LFP) battery-cell gigafactory (~1,000 direct jobs) at Pima County's Aerospace Research Campus south of Tucson, AZ. Most recent status (CurrentCells, Mar 25, 2026): still pre-full-construction — ABF secured 4.5+ GWh binding offtake, expects construction financing by mid-2026 and production start late 2027.

Chobani announced Sep 1, 2026 an ~$1.2B investment over five years to build a 1.5M-sq-ft dairy manufacturing and warehouse campus in Allentown, PA (Upper Macungie Township), creating 900+ jobs, by acquiring Keurig Dr Pepper's Allentown facility for $125M and converting it to produce high-protein/low-sugar milk products. Most recent status (Jax Daily Record, Aug 31, 2026): environmental permitting and interim R&D space underway; full factory construction now slated to begin in 2028 with production/deliveries targeted for 2030.

Silfab Solar announced on Sep 19, 2023 a $150M solar cell and PV module manufacturing plant (~785,000 sq ft; ~1 GW cell / 1.2 GW module capacity) in Fort Mill (York County), South Carolina, creating 800 direct jobs. Most recent status (Fort Mill Sun, Jul 31, 2026): the plant reached production, but temporarily idled its cell and module lines Aug 5-11, 2026 citing material/component supply constraints; the site is also subject to ongoing York County zoning litigation.

T1 Energy announced (June 2025) its ~$850M planned 5 GW G2_Austin solar cell factory (2.1 GW Phase 1) in Rockdale, Milam County, Texas, expected to create up to 1,800 direct jobs; construction began Dec 2025. This is a distinct facility from T1's G1 module plant in Wilmer/Dallas. Most recent status (pv-tech, Aug 14, 2026): Phase 1 building ready for interior MEP, first production-line equipment arriving at U.S. ports, Phase I capex raised to $510M, and first cell production now targeted Q1 2027 (slipped from an original H2 2026 goal).

JST Corp. (Japan Solderless Terminal) announced in April 2026 a $500M, 540,000-sq-ft electronic-connector manufacturing and design facility on a new 240-acre site at Conners Island Business Park in Guntersville (Marshall County), Alabama (~80 direct jobs; qualifies on the $500M capital floor). The project was first floated in December 2024 and formally sited in April 2026. Most recent status (WAFF, Apr 20 2026): groundbreaking expected as soon as the following month, with completion targeted for early 2029 — i.e., pre-/early-construction with no production yet.

Vital Farms announced in June 2024 a new egg washing and packing facility (its second, after Springfield, MO) in Seymour (Jackson County), Indiana. Most recent status (Hoosier Ag Today, Dec 18 2025): the project, now named Vital Crossroads (VXR), was expanded to a ~$250M investment (facility plus company-owned farms in Crawford and Lawrence counties), to be built in one phase rather than phases, with ~400 direct jobs expected by mid-2027; it broke ground mid-2025 and is targeted to be fully operational at the beginning of 2027 (under construction, not yet producing).

Ascend Elements announced in August 2022 plans to invest ~$310M in Phase 1 (up to ~$1B across phases) in 'Apex 1,' North America's first sustainable EV battery-materials (precursor cathode active material, pCAM) manufacturing facility in Hopkinsville (Christian County), Kentucky, projected at up to ~400 direct jobs; construction began October 2022. Most recent status (Recycling Today, Oct 2025): construction has been paused since late 2024 and federal support was cut — a $164M CAM grant was cancelled (Feb 2025) and the DOE rescinded much of a ~$316M grant (2025) — with the plant scaled back to pCAM and lithium carbonate only, restart expected in 2026 and operation targeted for Q3 2026 (not yet producing).

Cleveland-Cliffs (then Cliffs Natural Resources) announced on June 15, 2017 the site selection and development of its first hot briquetted iron (HBI) / direct-reduction plant in Toledo, Ohio — a ~$700M investment with ~1.6-1.9 million-tonne/year capacity and ~140 direct jobs (qualifies on the ~$700M capital floor). This is a distinct facility from Cliffs' Middletown Works. The plant was commissioned in mid-2020. Most recent status (Steel Market Update, Oct 23 2025): the plant is operating (it produced ~1.6 million metric tons of HBI during 2025 per Cliffs' FY2025 annual report) and Cliffs has weighed selling it as a non-core asset but is deprioritizing a sale for now.
